cb_topics: Anybody else see the IBM announcement? $1565 for 16K. SIXTEEN K.
My TRS-80 has more memory than that base model, and I paid less in '79.
VisiCalc on an IBM. That is the whole ballgame for business users.
CP/M-86 costs how much more than DOS? Kildall must be fuming.
Gas is over a buck thirty here. Remember when it was fifty cents?
Who is watching Dallas this fall? Sue Ellen had better behave.

headlines.summary: IBM announced its smallest, lowest-priced computer, the IBM Personal Computer, at a New York press conference this morning. The base system, with 16K of memory and BASIC built in, sells for $1,565 through ComputerLand dealers, Sears business machine stores, and IBM sales centers.
headlines.title: IBM ENTERS PERSONAL COMPUTER MARKET

headlines.summary: The system uses an Intel 8088 processor running at 4.77 megahertz. Buyers may choose PC-DOS from Microsoft for $40, CP/M-86 from Digital Research, or the UCSD p-System. VisiCalc and Peachtree business software were named among the programs available at launch.
headlines.title: NEW IBM MACHINE RUNS MICROSOFT DOS

headlines.summary: Byte magazine called the machine 'one of the most important announcements we have seen in the industry.' Apple answered with a full-page Wall Street Journal advertisement reading 'Welcome, IBM. Seriously,' welcoming the giant to the personal computer business.
headlines.title: INDUSTRY REACTS TO IBM ANNOUNCEMENT

headlines.summary: Breaking with its closed-system tradition, IBM is publishing a Technical Reference manual with BIOS listings and expansion schematics, and will sell its own line of plug-in expansion boards for the new machine.
headlines.title: IBM OPENS MACHINE TO DEVELOPERS

headlines.summary: Congress has sent the President the Economic Recovery Tax Act, the largest tax cut in American history, calling for a 25 percent across-the-board reduction phased in over three years. Signing is expected this week at his California ranch.
headlines.title: REAGAN TAX CUT AWAITS PRESIDENT'S SIGNATURE

headlines.summary: More than 11,000 air traffic controllers remain off the job after President Reagan ordered striking PATCO members fired last week. Military controllers and supervisors are handling commercial traffic, and airlines are flying reduced schedules.
headlines.title: AIR CONTROLLERS STRIKE ENTERS SECOND WEEK

headlines.summary: Major league baseball resumed this week after a 50-day players' strike, with the All-Star Game played Sunday in Cleveland. Owners and players agreed to a split-season format with an extra round of playoffs.
headlines.title: BASEBALL BACK AFTER PLAYERS' STRIKE

headlines.summary: MTV: Music Television began cablecasting August 1 with the Buggles' 'Video Killed the Radio Star.' The Warner-Amex channel programs rock videos around the clock.
headlines.title: CABLE VIEWERS GET ALL-MUSIC CHANNEL

headlines.summary: Solidarity, the independent Polish labor federation, continues pressing the Warsaw government for economic reforms amid food shortages and labor unrest.
headlines.title: POLISH UNION PRESSURES WARSAW GOVERNMENT

headlines.summary: The Federal Reserve's tight-money campaign keeps the prime lending rate near 20 percent as the central bank battles double-digit inflation. Business borrowing costs remain at historic highs.
headlines.title: PRIME RATE HOLDS NEAR 20 PERCENT

1981-08-12.label: IBM PC announced
market_notes: Prime rate near 20% as Volcker's Federal Reserve squeezes inflation; business borrowing at historic cost.
IBM shares watched closely after the PC announcement; analysts debate whether Big Blue can move fast in the microcomputer market.

on_this_day.summary: MTV: Music Television began cablecasting with 'Video Killed the Radio Star.'

announcements: NEW: The Macintosh Owners Forum is now open -- GO MAC. Tips, desk accessories, and software notes for Apple's new machine.

cb_topics: The Mac talked! Did anyone else read about the shareholders meeting?
$2495 for 128K and no hard disk. My PC-XT laughs.
A mouse. Icons. No more DOS commands to memorize. My wife could use this.
That 1984 commercial during the Super Bowl -- the hammer throw! Best ad ever.
Raiders killed the Redskins. 38-9. Marcus Allen is unreal.
Long distance is a mess since the breakup. MCI keeps calling me at dinner.

headlines.summary: Apple Computer introduced the Macintosh at its annual shareholders meeting in Cupertino today. The $2,495 machine replaces typed commands with a mouse, icons, and pull-down menus on a 9-inch black-and-white display.
headlines.title: APPLE UNVEILS MACINTOSH

headlines.summary: In a flourish, Steven Jobs had the machine introduce itself in synthesized speech before a cheering audience: 'Never trust a computer you can't lift!' The demonstration drew a standing ovation.
headlines.title: 'HELLO, I'M MACINTOSH'

headlines.summary: Motorola 68000 processor at 8 megahertz, 128K of memory, a 3.5-inch 400K floppy drive, and bundled MacWrite and MacPaint software. There is no hard disk; a second floppy drive is optional.
headlines.title: MACINTOSH SPECIFICATIONS DETAILED

headlines.summary: Two days before the unveiling, Apple's Ridley Scott-directed '1984' commercial aired during Super Bowl XVIII. The Los Angeles Raiders defeated Washington 38-9 at Tampa Stadium before more than 77 million viewers.
headlines.title: APPLE'S '1984' AD STUNS SUPER BOWL VIEWERS

headlines.summary: The AT&T divestiture became effective January 1, spinning off seven regional Bell companies. Long-distance customers are choosing among AT&T, MCI, and Sprint for the first time.
headlines.title: BELL SYSTEM BREAKUP TAKES EFFECT

headlines.summary: U.S. Marines remain at the Beirut airport as part of the multinational force, months after the October barracks bombing killed 241 American servicemen.
headlines.title: MARINES HOLD BEIRUT POSITIONS

headlines.summary: Astronomers are preparing for Halley's Comet, due at perihelion in February 1986, with an international armada of spacecraft planned for close encounters.
headlines.title: ASTRONOMERS AWAIT HALLEY'S COMET

headlines.summary: Marcus Allen ran for 191 yards and two touchdowns as Los Angeles won 38-9 at Tampa Stadium on Sunday, the most lopsided Super Bowl yet played.
headlines.title: RAIDERS ROUT REDSKINS IN SUPER BOWL

headlines.summary: The spreadsheet program remains the must-have business application, moving IBM-compatible hardware off dealer shelves as offices automate.
headlines.title: LOTUS 1-2-3 DRIVES PC SALES

headlines.summary: The Yugoslavian city is readying venues for the Winter Olympics, opening February 8 with athletes from dozens of nations.
headlines.title: SARAJEVO PREPARES FOR WINTER GAMES

1984-01-24.label: Apple Macintosh debuts

AT&T begins life as a long-distance company; the seven regional Bells open separately. Dividend checks will look different this quarter.

on_this_day.summary: The Ridley Scott spot runs during Super Bowl XVIII.

on_this_day.summary: The Bell System splits into AT&T and seven regional companies.

on_this_day.summary: James Marshall's find sets off the California Gold Rush.

1985-07-13.label: Live Aid

headlines.title: LIVE AID ROCKS WEMBLEY AND JFK STADIUM
headlines.summary: Bob Geldof and Midge Ure's 16-hour dual-venue benefit concert is underway at London's Wembley Stadium and Philadelphia's JFK Stadium. Some 72,000 fans are at Wembley and roughly 90,000 in Philadelphia for what organizers are calling a 'global jukebox' against famine in Africa.

headlines.title: 13 SATELLITES BEAM CONCERT TO MORE THAN 110 NATIONS
headlines.summary: Using 13 satellites and 22 transponders, the concerts are being broadcast live to more than 110 countries, with organizers saying as many as 1.9 billion people may tune in -- one of the largest television audiences in history.

headlines.title: QUEEN STEALS THE SHOW AT WEMBLEY
headlines.summary: Freddie Mercury and Queen captivated Wembley with a 20-minute hit-filled set, from 'Bohemian Rhapsody' to 'We Are the Champions' -- already being called the performance of the day.

headlines.title: PHIL COLLINS' CONCORDE DOUBLE-DUTY
headlines.summary: Phil Collins played Wembley this afternoon, boarded the Concorde, and took the Philadelphia stage this evening -- then sat in on drums for a reunion of the surviving members of Led Zeppelin.

headlines.title: FAMINE RELIEF PLEDGE LINES JAMMED
headlines.summary: Telephone donation lines in more than 40 countries are taking pledges for Ethiopian famine relief during the broadcast. The concert follows December's Band Aid single 'Do They Know It's Christmas?' and was organized by Geldof and Ure in just ten weeks.

headlines.title: REAGAN RECOVERING AFTER CANCER SURGERY
headlines.summary: President Reagan underwent surgery at Bethesda Naval Hospital this morning to remove a cancerous polyp from his colon. Doctors say the operation went well; the President is expected to resume duties within days.

headlines.title: COCA-COLA BRINGS BACK THE ORIGINAL FORMULA
headlines.summary: After 79 days of consumer protest, Coca-Cola announced this week it will sell the original formula again as 'Coke Classic' alongside New Coke -- one of the fastest reversals in corporate history.

headlines.title: ALL-STAR GAME TUESDAY AT THE METRODOME
headlines.summary: Baseball's best gather Tuesday in Minneapolis for the All-Star Game, with the National League looking to extend its recent dominance over the American League.

headlines.title: BACK TO THE FUTURE LEADS SUMMER BOX OFFICE
headlines.summary: Michael J. Fox's time-travel comedy, released last week, is the summer's runaway hit, with the DeLorean already the most talked-about car in America.

headlines.title: GORBACHEV'S ANTI-DRINKING DRIVE SWEEPS SOVIET UNION
headlines.summary: The new Soviet leader's campaign against alcoholism has cut vodka production and raised prices, prompting long lines and grumbling from Moscow to Vladivostok.

CB Simulator: Channel 5 is the Live Aid channel today. All handles welcome -- keep it friendly.

cb_topics: Queen just played the set of the decade. Freddie Mercury owns Wembley.
Phil Collins did London AND Philly in one day. The Concorde is cheating.
Did you get through on the donation line? Busy signal for an hour here.
They keep cutting from London to Philly and I keep missing the good parts.
Back to the Future last weekend -- the DeLorean! Best movie in years.
Hope Reagan is all right. The surgery news came out of nowhere.
market_notes: Wall Street is closed for the weekend; Friday's session was quiet ahead of today's concert headlines.
Coca-Cola shares in focus after the company bowed to pressure and brought back the original formula as Coke Classic.

on_this_day.title: Live Aid rocks Wembley and JFK Stadium (July 13, 1985)

announcements: A message from the sysops: our thoughts are with the families of the Challenger crew, and with the teachers and students who followed this mission. Tonight's CB conference will observe a moment of silence.
The Space/Astronomy forum has opened a memorial thread for Challenger. Please keep discussion respectful.
NASA mission summaries are being added to the reference library as they become available.
cb_topics: I watched it happen live. My kids' classroom went silent. I do not have words.
Christa McAuliffe was supposed to teach lessons from orbit. My daughter wrote her a letter.
Reagan speaks tonight. 'Slipped the surly bonds of earth.' I am not ashamed to say I cried.
The Bears won the Super Bowl Sunday. Feels like a month ago already.
Does anyone know if the shuttle program will fly again? My son keeps asking.
Gas is under a dollar here for the first time in years. Small mercies.

headlines.summary: The space shuttle Challenger broke apart 73 seconds after liftoff from Kennedy Space Center this morning, killing all seven aboard. The crew included Christa McAuliffe, the New Hampshire teacher chosen as the first private citizen in space.
headlines.title: SHUTTLE CHALLENGER LOST AFTER LIFTOFF

headlines.summary: The President set aside tonight's address to Congress, declaring 'today is a day for mourning and remembering,' and will speak to the nation from the Oval Office this evening.
headlines.title: REAGAN POSTPONES STATE OF THE UNION

headlines.summary: Commander Francis Scobee, pilot Michael Smith, mission specialists Judith Resnik, Ellison Onizuka and Ronald McNair, and payload specialists Gregory Jarvis and Christa McAuliffe.
headlines.title: THE CREW OF STS-51L

headlines.summary: The launch went ahead despite overnight temperatures near freezing, the coldest shuttle launch yet. NASA officials say it is too early to know whether the cold played a role; a board of inquiry is being appointed.
headlines.title: QUESTIONS ABOUT COLD-WEATHER LAUNCH

headlines.summary: Millions of schoolchildren watched live as McAuliffe, 37, a social studies teacher from Concord, New Hampshire, was to teach two lessons from orbit during the mission.
headlines.title: SCHOOLS MOURN TEACHER IN SPACE

headlines.summary: Chicago defeated New England 46-10 Sunday at the Superdome, capping a dominant season. William 'The Refrigerator' Perry scored a touchdown.

headlines.summary: The comet reaches its closest approach to the sun next month; spacecraft from the Soviet Union, Japan, and Europe are closing in for encounters.
headlines.title: HALLEY'S COMET NEARS PERIHELION

headlines.summary: Crude oil continues its slide as OPEC members pump beyond quotas, squeezing Texas producers and alarming energy lenders.
headlines.title: OIL PRICES SLIDE BELOW $20

headlines.title: AQUINO CAMPAIGNS IN PHILIPPINES

headlines.title: DESKTOP PUBLISHING GROWS

Defense and aerospace shares steady; investors await NASA's inquiry before reassessing shuttle contractors.

1986-04-26.label: Chernobyl

headlines.title: EXPLOSION REPORTED AT SOVIET NUCLEAR PLANT
headlines.summary: Western news agencies report an explosion and fire at the Chernobyl nuclear power station in the Ukrainian Soviet Socialist Republic, during a safety test at Reactor No. 4 in the early hours this morning. Details are fragmentary; the full scale of the accident is not yet known.

headlines.title: KREMLIN SILENT ON CHERNOBYL REPORTS
headlines.summary: Moscow has issued no statement about the reported accident. Soviet media carry no mention of Chernobyl, and Western governments say they are seeking confirmation through diplomatic channels.

headlines.title: FIREFIGHTERS BATTLE BLAZE AT REACTOR
headlines.summary: Scattered reports describe firefighters and plant workers hurt while fighting the fire at the damaged reactor. Casualty figures are unconfirmed; Soviet authorities have released no information.

headlines.title: EUROPEAN MONITORS WATCH FOR RADIATION
headlines.summary: Radiation monitoring stations across Scandinavia and Western Europe report nothing unusual so far, but scientists say the path of any release from the plant is unknown until Moscow discloses what happened.

headlines.title: NO WORD OF EVACUATION AT PRIPYAT
headlines.summary: There are no confirmed reports of evacuations from Pripyat, the plant workers' city of some 50,000 near the station. Residents are said to be going about a normal Saturday.

headlines.title: SHUTTLE FLEET STILL GROUNDED
headlines.summary: NASA's orbiters remain grounded nearly three months after Challenger. Engineers continue the investigation while a presidential commission prepares its findings.

headlines.title: AQUINO GOVERNMENT CONSOLIDATES IN MANILA
headlines.summary: Two months after Corazon Aquino took office, her government is working to stabilize the Philippines after the fall of Ferdinand Marcos.

headlines.title: IBM ENTERS PORTABLE COMPUTER MARKET
headlines.summary: IBM this month unveiled the PC Convertible, its first portable computer: about 13 pounds, dual 3.5-inch floppy drives, and a price of $1,995.

headlines.title: BASEBALL'S HOTTEST TEAM: THE METS
headlines.summary: New York's Mets are off to a torrid start, leading the National League East as April winds down.

headlines.title: TOP GUN ARRIVES NEXT MONTH
headlines.summary: Tom Cruise's Navy fighter-pilot drama Top Gun opens May 16, with advance buzz calling it the summer's likely blockbuster.

announcements: A note from the sysops: reports of a serious accident at a Soviet nuclear plant are unconfirmed and developing. Please treat rumors on the service with care until facts are established.
The World News forum has an open thread on today's reports from the Soviet Union -- GO WORLDNEWS. Please keep discussion factual and respectful.
New in the reference library: a fact file on nuclear power generation, added for members following today's news.
cb_topics: Reports of an explosion at a Soviet nuclear plant. No word from Moscow. This is frightening.
Fifty thousand people live next to that plant. Pray it is contained.
If they are not telling their own people, they are not telling us anything.
Glasnost is being tested tonight, and it is failing.
Oil is under twenty dollars and the shuttle fleet is grounded. What a spring.
market_notes: Markets are closed for the weekend; Friday's trading ended before any word of the Soviet accident emerged.
European markets showed little reaction Friday; traders say any response to Chernobyl will have to wait for Monday's open.

cb_topics: The Dow just fell 500 points. FIVE HUNDRED. Is my 401(k) gone?
My broker's line has been busy for two hours. TWO HOURS.
They are saying the computers did it -- program trading just kept selling.
And on the same day we are shelling Iranian oil platforms. What a Monday.
Twins are up 2-0 in the Series, at least. Small comfort.
My dad says he remembers '29. He says do not panic. Trying not to.

headlines.summary: The Dow Jones industrial average fell 508.32 points, or 22.6 percent, to 1,738.74 -- the largest one-day decline in Wall Street history, nearly double the 1929 record. A record 604 million shares changed hands.
headlines.title: DOW PLUNGES 508 POINTS IN HISTORIC CRASH

headlines.summary: Order systems were overwhelmed as the selloff accelerated; dozens of stocks faced delayed openings, and investors waited an hour or more for trade confirmations.
headlines.title: SELLING SWAMPS EXCHANGE SYSTEMS

headlines.summary: Computer-driven portfolio insurance strategies are blamed for accelerating the decline, turning a selloff into a cascade as programs dumped stock-index futures automatically.
headlines.title: PROGRAM TRADING BLAMED FOR CASCADE

headlines.summary: Panic circled the globe as exchanges from Hong Kong to London to Sydney posted heavy losses, with London's market suffering its worst week on record.
headlines.title: CRASH GOES GLOBAL

headlines.summary: The White House said the economy remains fundamentally sound. Treasury and Federal Reserve officials are in close contact as markets reel, and traders await word on emergency measures.
headlines.title: WASHINGTON RESPONDS TO MELTDOWN

headlines.summary: Navy warships shelled two Iranian oil platforms in the Persian Gulf in retaliation for last week's missile attack on the reflagged tanker Sea Isle City. President Reagan called it 'a prudent yet restrained response.'
headlines.title: U.S. DESTROYS IRANIAN OIL PLATFORMS

headlines.summary: Treasury Secretary James Baker's weekend threat to let the dollar fall further, after criticizing West Germany's interest-rate hike, deepened fears of a policy rift days before the crash.
headlines.title: BAKER'S DOLLAR REMARKS RATTLE MARKETS

headlines.summary: U.S. and Soviet negotiators are pressing toward an intermediate-range missile treaty ahead of a planned December summit between Reagan and Gorbachev.
headlines.title: ARMS TALKS PRESS TOWARD SUMMIT

headlines.summary: Minnesota took the first two games at the Metrodome over St. Louis; the Series resumes Tuesday night in Missouri.
headlines.title: TWINS LEAD WORLD SERIES 2-0

headlines.summary: IBM's PS/2 line, introduced this spring with the OS/2 operating system, faces a cautious market as businesses weigh the cost of upgrading.

headlines.summary: Brokerage phone lines jammed as individual investors tried to reach advisors, and mutual fund redemption orders piled up through the afternoon.

Portfolio insurance and program trading identified as accelerants; dollar policy and trade-deficit fears as triggers.

1989-03-24.label: Exxon Valdez

headlines.title: TANKER RUNS AGROUND, SPILLING OIL OFF ALASKA
headlines.summary: The supertanker Exxon Valdez struck Bligh Reef in Prince William Sound shortly after midnight, tearing open its hull. The ship was carrying 53 million gallons of North Slope crude; an estimated 11 million gallons are spilling into the sound.

headlines.title: SLICK SPREADS THROUGH PRISTINE SOUND
headlines.summary: The Coast Guard has closed the Port of Valdez to tanker traffic. Alyeska, the pipeline consortium, has taken charge of the initial response; containment crews are working against wind and cold in the remote sound.

headlines.title: WILDLIFE AND FISHERIES IN PERIL
headlines.summary: Prince William Sound is one of North America's richest marine habitats. Sea otters, harbor seals, millions of migratory birds, and the herring and salmon fisheries that sustain coastal communities all lie in the slick's path.

headlines.title: CAPTAIN QUESTIONED AS PROBE BEGINS
headlines.summary: The Coast Guard is questioning Captain Joseph Hazelwood and the crew. Early questions focus on why the 987-foot tanker left the outbound shipping lane to avoid ice; Exxon says the cause remains under investigation.

headlines.title: CLEANUP FACES REMOTE, RUGGED WATERS
headlines.summary: The sound is reachable only by boat and helicopter. Alyeska's contingency plans -- booms, skimmers, and dispersants -- are being tested at a scale no one planned for.

headlines.title: ALASKA LEADERS DEMAND ANSWERS
headlines.summary: State officials are pressing Exxon and Alyeska for a full account of the response effort. The spill threatens the livelihood of fishing towns around the sound as the spring season approaches.

headlines.title: CERN PHYSICIST PROPOSES WEB OF NOTES
headlines.summary: Tim Berners-Lee at CERN has circulated a proposal for a hypertext 'web' of information shared across computer networks. For now it is just a memo.

headlines.title: MARCH MADNESS REACHES REGIONAL FINALS
headlines.summary: The NCAA tournament narrows to eight teams this weekend, with regional finals set for Saturday and Sunday.

headlines.title: SOVIETS OUT OF AFGHANISTAN
headlines.summary: Soviet troops completed their withdrawal from Afghanistan last month, ending nearly a decade of war.

headlines.title: OSCAR NIGHT IS WEDNESDAY; RAIN MAN THE FAVORITE
headlines.summary: Hollywood gathers Wednesday for the Academy Awards, with Rain Man expected to take Best Picture over Working Girl and Mississippi Burning.

The pictures of the otters -- I cannot look at them.
Who pays for this? Exxon will be writing checks for years.
Fishing season is ruined for those towns. Generations of work, gone.
Rain Man for Best Picture on Wednesday. Feels strange to care about that today.

CB Simulator: Channel 1 is hosting an open discussion on tonight's events in Germany. All members welcome.
New in the reference library: a Germany fact file with maps of Berlin's crossing points.
cb_topics: Are you watching Berlin? People are standing ON the Wall. ON it.
My cousin was stationed in West Berlin in the 70s. He says he is crying.
Schabowski just... announced it by accident? Unbelievable.
Wilder won in Virginia and Dinkins in New York. What a week.
My kid wants a Game Boy for Christmas. So does every kid in America.
The A's swept the Series and now this. October and November have been unreal.

headlines.summary: East German authorities announced this evening that citizens may travel to the West effective immediately. Thousands massed at border crossings in Berlin, and overwhelmed guards opened the gates. Crowds are celebrating atop the Wall tonight.
headlines.title: EAST GERMANY OPENS THE WALL

headlines.summary: Politburo spokesman Guenter Schabowski, handed new travel regulations he had not been briefed on, told a televised press conference the rules take effect 'immediately, without delay.' Within the hour, East Berliners were streaming toward the crossings.
headlines.title: SCHABOWSKI ANNOUNCEMENT IGNITES EXODUS

headlines.summary: Border guards, who had received no clear orders, yielded to the crowds late in the evening as chants of 'Open the gate!' rose at checkpoints across the divided city.
headlines.title: CROSSINGS OVERWHELMED LATE TONIGHT

headlines.summary: President Bush welcomed the development but struck a cautious note, saying he would not 'dance on the Berlin Wall.' In Moscow, Soviet officials offered no objection as the night unfolded.
headlines.title: BUSH WELCOMES OPENING, URGES CALM

headlines.summary: In Tuesday's elections, L. Douglas Wilder became the first elected black governor in American history in Virginia, and David Dinkins became New York City's first black mayor.
headlines.title: WILDER, DINKINS MAKE HISTORY IN U.S. VOTE

headlines.summary: European markets took the Berlin news in stride; analysts are weighing what open borders and reunification talk mean for the continent's economy.
headlines.title: MARKETS STEADY AS EUROPE SHIFTS

headlines.summary: Nintendo's handheld, launched in the U.S. this summer with Tetris packed in, is the season's must-have toy as the holidays approach.
headlines.title: GAME BOY CONQUERS PLAYGROUNDS

headlines.summary: The Bay Area continues cleanup from the October 17 Loma Prieta earthquake, which killed 63 people and collapsed a section of the Bay Bridge.
headlines.title: QUAKE RECOVERY CONTINUES IN CALIFORNIA

headlines.summary: Oakland completed a four-game sweep of San Francisco in the World Series, played ten days late after the earthquake interrupted it.
headlines.title: A'S SWEEP GIANTS IN QUAKE-DELAYED SERIES

headlines.summary: The Galileo spacecraft, launched last month aboard the shuttle Atlantis, is on its six-year voyage to Jupiter.
headlines.title: GALILEO EN ROUTE TO JUPITER

1989-11-09.label: Berlin Wall falls
market_notes: West German markets steady; traders debate what open borders mean for European growth.
U.S. markets little changed; analysts say the week's U.S. election results matter more to domestic stocks.

on_this_day.summary: Anti-Jewish violence erupts across Germany; synagogues and shops destroyed.
on_this_day.title: Kristallnacht pogroms begin (November 9, 1938)

on_this_day.summary: A massive power failure darkens New York and much of the Northeast.
on_this_day.title: Northeast blackout (November 9, 1965)

on_this_day.summary: East Germany announces free travel; crowds stream through the crossings.
on_this_day.title: Berlin Wall opened (November 9, 1989)

1991-01-17.label: Desert Storm begins

headlines.title: COALITION AIR STRIKES POUND IRAQ
headlines.summary: Operation Desert Storm began in the early hours of this morning, Baghdad time, as hundreds of coalition aircraft struck targets across Iraq and occupied Kuwait. President Bush announced the offensive in a televised address last night, hours after the United Nations deadline passed.

headlines.title: 'THE LIBERATION OF KUWAIT HAS BEGUN,' BUSH DECLARES
headlines.summary: Speaking from the Oval Office, the President said the coalition acted after Iraq defied the U.N. deadline to withdraw from Kuwait. Congress authorized the use of force last Saturday.

headlines.title: BAGHDAD LIT BY ANTI-AIRCRAFT FIRE
headlines.summary: Television networks are broadcasting live from Baghdad, where tracer fire fills the night sky. Early reports describe strikes on air defenses, airfields, and command centers; coalition losses are not yet known.

headlines.title: 32 NATIONS STAND WITH THE COALITION
headlines.summary: General Norman Schwarzkopf commands a force that includes more than 415,000 American troops, alongside British, French, Saudi, Egyptian, and other allied forces massed in Saudi Arabia.

headlines.title: SADDAM VOWED 'MOTHER OF ALL BATTLES'
headlines.summary: Iraq's leader had promised a devastating response to any attack. Attention now turns to whether Baghdad will fire Scud missiles at Israel or Saudi Arabia in retaliation.

headlines.title: PATRIOT BATTERIES DEPLOYED TO ISRAEL
headlines.summary: U.S. Patriot missile batteries rushed to Israel and Saudi Arabia stand ready against possible Scud attacks; civil defense drills have been held across Israel this week.

headlines.title: SOVIET TROOPS STORM VILNIUS TV TOWER
headlines.summary: Fourteen Lithuanians were killed Sunday when Soviet forces seized the television tower in Vilnius. President Gorbachev faces condemnation abroad and a deepening crisis at home.

headlines.title: SUPER BOWL XXV TEN DAYS AWAY
headlines.summary: The New York Giants and Buffalo Bills meet January 27 in Tampa, with the nation at war for the first championship game of the decade.

headlines.title: RECESSION DEEPENS AS WAR BEGINS
headlines.summary: The economy, already in recession since last summer, faces new uncertainty; unemployment topped 6 percent in December and forecasters see no quick rebound.

headlines.title: NOTEBOOK COMPUTERS RACE BELOW $3,000
headlines.summary: PC makers are rushing lightweight notebook machines to market as prices fall, chasing the road warriors who once lugged 15-pound luggables.

announcements: The World News forum has an open thread on the Gulf war -- GO WORLDNEWS. Please keep discussion respectful; many members have family in the region.
CB Simulator: Channel 1 is hosting discussion of tonight's events. A moment of silence for the troops opens the hour.
New in the reference library: Gulf region maps and a guide to following war news on the service.
cb_topics: Watching Baghdad live on CNN. Tracers over the city. I cannot believe this is real.
My brother is with the 101st. If anyone hears unit news, please post it.
Bush sounded grim tonight. 'This will not stand' -- now we will see.
Gas was $1.25 yesterday. What happens to prices now?
Ten days to the Super Bowl and it feels like the wrong planet.
Patriots in Tel Aviv. Pray the Scuds stay in their bunkers.
market_notes: Oil prices plunged more than $10 a barrel as the air campaign opened and Western nations moved to release strategic reserves; crude settled near $21.
The Dow posted a triple-digit gain as the 'war premium' drained out of oil and investors bet on a swift campaign.
Defense and aerospace shares rallied; airline stocks rebounded on hopes for cheaper jet fuel.
Gold, the classic haven, fell as the fighting began without an immediate Iraqi counterstrike.

on_this_day.title: Operation Desert Storm air campaign begins (January 17, 1991)
on_this_day.summary: Coalition aircraft strike Iraq and occupied Kuwait after the U.N. deadline passes.

on_this_day.title: Eisenhower warns of the 'military-industrial complex' (January 17, 1961)
on_this_day.summary: In his farewell address, the President cautions against unwarranted influence by the defense establishment.

on_this_day.title: Prohibition takes effect in the United States (January 17, 1920)
on_this_day.summary: The Volstead Act takes effect, banning the manufacture and sale of intoxicating liquor.

announcements: NEW: The Internet SIG is now open -- GO INTERNET. Discussion of TCP/IP tools, Gopher, and the new WorldWideWeb project from CERN.
The file library has a new Internet section with FTP site lists and protocol documents.
CB Simulator: Channel 9 hosts a weekly Internet roundtable, Thursdays at 9 PM Eastern.
cb_topics: Some fellow at CERN posted about a 'WorldWideWeb.' Hypertext over the Internet. Anyone tried it?
You need a NeXT to run his browser. A NeXT! Who has ten grand?
Gopher is easier. Menus, no fancy formatting. This web thing is a toy.
START treaty signed. Maybe the Cold War is really over.
Terminator 2 last month -- the liquid metal fellow. Best effects I have ever seen.
Gas is $1.14 here and I am supposed to be happy about it?

headlines.summary: Tim Berners-Lee, a computer scientist at CERN in Geneva, posted a public invitation on the alt.hypertext newsgroup today describing the WorldWideWeb project: a hypertext system for sharing information across the Internet. The first site runs on his NeXT computer at info.cern.ch.
headlines.title: CERN PHYSICIST INVITES WORLD TO 'WEB'

headlines.summary: Berners-Lee's system links documents with hypertext using new protocols called HTTP and HTML. Readers need his WorldWideWeb browser program, now publicly available, to follow the links between documents.
headlines.title: WHAT IS THE WORLDWIDEWEB?

headlines.summary: The University of Minnesota's Gopher protocol, released this spring, offers a simpler, menu-driven rival for finding information on the Internet -- and currently has far more users than the new Web.
headlines.title: GOPHER OFFERS MENU-DRIVEN RIVAL

headlines.summary: Presidents Bush and Gorbachev signed the Strategic Arms Reduction Treaty last week in Moscow, limiting each side to 6,000 nuclear warheads. The Senate must still ratify it.
headlines.title: START TREATY SIGNED IN MOSCOW

headlines.summary: Soviet conservatives are criticizing Gorbachev's reforms as the republics press for sovereignty, raising questions about the reformer's hold on power.
headlines.title: GORBACHEV FACES HARD-LINE PRESSURE

headlines.summary: Unemployment remains above 6.5 percent as the nation waits to see whether the recession that began last summer has truly ended.
headlines.title: ECONOMY SHOWS MIXED SIGNALS

headlines.summary: With two months to play, division races are tightening across both leagues as contenders jockey for October.
headlines.title: BASEBALL PENNANT RACES TIGHTEN

headlines.summary: Microsoft's latest DOS adds task swapping, an improved BASIC, and a full-screen editor, with upgrade pricing under $100.
headlines.title: MS-DOS 5.0 SHIPS TO DEALERS

headlines.summary: Clarence Thomas's Supreme Court nomination awaits fall confirmation hearings after his July selection to replace Thurgood Marshall.
headlines.title: THOMAS NOMINATION AWAITS FALL HEARINGS

headlines.summary: Astronomers are designing corrective optics for the Hubble Space Telescope's flawed mirror, with a shuttle repair mission planned for the coming years.
headlines.title: HUBBLE TEAMS PLAN MIRROR REPAIR

1991-08-06.label: first website public invitation
market_notes: Stocks drift as investors parse mixed economic data; unemployment stuck above 6.5%.
Technology shares mixed; Microsoft's DOS 5.0 launch draws dealer interest.

on_this_day.summary: The first combat use of an atomic weapon devastates the Japanese city.
on_this_day.title: Atomic bomb dropped on Hiroshima (August 6, 1945)

on_this_day.summary: The Security Council imposes sweeping sanctions after the invasion of Kuwait.
on_this_day.title: U.N. sanctions Iraq (August 6, 1990)

on_this_day.summary: Tim Berners-Lee posts a public invitation to the Web project on alt.hypertext.
on_this_day.title: WorldWideWeb opened to the public (August 6, 1991)

1981-04-12.label: Columbia's first flight

headlines.title: COLUMBIA LIFTS OFF ON FIRST SHUTTLE MISSION
headlines.summary: Space Shuttle Columbia lifted off from Launch Complex 39A at Kennedy Space Center at 7 a.m. Eastern today, carrying astronauts John Young and Robert Crippen on the maiden flight of the Space Shuttle program. The launch came exactly 20 years to the day after Yuri Gagarin's first human spaceflight.

headlines.title: YOUNG AND CRIPPEN: VETERAN AND ROOKIE
headlines.summary: Mission Commander John Young is making his fifth spaceflight -- he walked on the Moon during Apollo 16. Pilot Robert Crippen, a Navy test pilot, is flying in space for the first time. Their 54-hour test flight will wring out the orbiter's systems before a planned Tuesday landing at Edwards Air Force Base.

headlines.title: SHUTTLE STACK: ORBITER, TANK, TWIN BOOSTERS
headlines.summary: The shuttle leaves the pad as a three-part stack: the Columbia orbiter with its 30,000 heat-resistant tiles, a giant external fuel tank, and two solid rocket boosters. Today marks the first time a crewed vehicle has flown its maiden voyage with a crew aboard.

headlines.title: TODAY'S LAUNCH FOLLOWS FRIDAY SCRUB
headlines.summary: Friday's first launch attempt was scrubbed by a computer timing glitch during the countdown. Engineers corrected the error and recycled the count, and this morning's countdown ran cleanly to liftoff.

headlines.title: REAGAN BACK AT WHITE HOUSE AFTER SHOOTING
headlines.summary: President Reagan returned to the White House yesterday, less than two weeks after being wounded by a gunman outside the Washington Hilton. Doctors say the President is recovering well and resuming a light schedule.

headlines.title: REAGAN TAX PLAN ADVANCES IN CONGRESS
headlines.summary: The President's supply-side tax-cut proposal is moving through Congress, with supporters promising it will spur investment and critics warning of ballooning deficits. The plan would cut personal rates by 30 percent over three years.

headlines.title: POLAND'S SOLIDARITY STANDS FIRM
headlines.summary: Lech Walesa's independent Solidarity labor federation continues pressing Poland's government for economic reforms, eight months after the strikes that won the union legal recognition.

headlines.title: FERNANDOMANIA SWEEPS BASEBALL'S FIRST WEEK
headlines.summary: Dodgers rookie Fernando Valenzuela, a 20-year-old left-hander from Mexico, opened the season with a shutout and has yet to allow a run. The baseball season is under way across both leagues.

headlines.title: 'KISS ON MY LIST' TOPS THE CHARTS
headlines.summary: Hall and Oates' 'Kiss on My List' holds the number one spot on the pop charts, ahead of a spring field of new releases.

headlines.title: EDWARDS AFB READIES FOR TUESDAY LANDING
headlines.summary: Crews at Edwards Air Force Base in California are preparing the dry lakebed runway for Columbia's planned Tuesday touchdown, which would cap the first shuttle mission with a landing no capsule could attempt.

announcements: SPACE FORUM: STS-1 mission coverage -- GO SPACE. Track Columbia's first flight with the crew's progress reports.
CB Simulator: Channel 9 is the shuttle channel this weekend. Keep your CB chatter friendly.
Scheduled maintenance: the service will be unavailable Sunday 2:00-6:00 AM Eastern for system upgrades.
cb_topics: Columbia went up at 7 AM Eastern! Did anyone catch the launch on the morning news?
Twenty years to the day after Gagarin. You cannot make that up.
Young walked on the Moon. Now he is flying a truck with wings. Legend.
30,000 tiles and a maiden voyage with a crew aboard. That is bold.
Two days up there just to test the systems. Then they land it like a glider.
Gas is over a buck thirty here. The future is expensive.
market_notes: Wall Street is closed for the weekend; traders eye Monday after a week of inflation worry.
Rockwell International shares in focus as its Columbia orbiter makes the shuttle program's maiden flight.

on_this_day.title: Columbia's STS-1 lifts off from Kennedy Space Center (April 12, 1981)
on_this_day.summary: John Young and Robert Crippen ride the first Space Shuttle mission, 20 years to the day after Gagarin's flight.

on_this_day.title: Yuri Gagarin becomes the first human in space (April 12, 1961)
on_this_day.summary: The Soviet cosmonaut completes one 108-minute orbit of Earth aboard Vostok 1.

on_this_day.title: Franklin D. Roosevelt dies in Warm Springs (April 12, 1945)
on_this_day.summary: Harry Truman is sworn in as president hours later.

1987-12-08.label: INF Treaty signed

headlines.title: REAGAN AND GORBACHEV SIGN INF TREATY
headlines.summary: President Reagan and Soviet leader Mikhail Gorbachev signed the Intermediate-Range Nuclear Forces Treaty at the White House this afternoon, agreeing to eliminate all land-based missiles with ranges of 500 to 5,500 kilometers. It is the first arms treaty to require the destruction of existing weapons.

headlines.title: SUMMIT CROWDS GREET GORBACHEV IN WASHINGTON
headlines.summary: Thousands lined the Soviet leader's motorcade route through the capital as Gorbachev made his first visit to Washington. Reagan quoted a Russian proverb at the signing: 'Trust, but verify.'

headlines.title: PERSHING AND SS-20 MISSILES HEADED FOR SCRAP
headlines.summary: The treaty's double-zero formula covers American Pershing II and cruise missiles in Europe and Soviet SS-20 missiles. Nearly 2,700 missiles are to be destroyed within three years under intrusive on-site inspection.

headlines.title: AFGHANISTAN TOPS SUMMIT SIDEBAR
headlines.summary: President Reagan pressed Gorbachev for a timetable to withdraw Soviet troops from Afghanistan, where the war is in its eighth year. Aides say the two leaders made progress but reached no final agreement.

headlines.title: WALL STREET STEADIES AFTER BLACK MONDAY
headlines.summary: Stocks held their ground in light holiday trading, extending a seven-week climb back from the October 19 crash. The Dow remains well below its August peak as investors eye the new year.

headlines.title: IBM AND MICROSOFT SHIP OS/2
headlines.summary: IBM's OS/2 operating system, developed with Microsoft for the Personal System/2 line, is reaching dealers this month. The new system promises multitasking and access to memory beyond the 640K DOS limit.

headlines.title: MACINTOSH II BRINGS COLOR TO THE MAC
headlines.summary: Apple's Macintosh II, introduced this spring, is winning over desktop publishers with its color display and open slots -- at prices that can top $5,000 fully loaded.

headlines.title: NFL PLAYOFF RACES ENTER FINAL WEEKS
headlines.summary: With the regular season winding down, the 49ers, Redskins, and Bears pace the playoff field after a strike-disrupted autumn that saw replacement players take the field in October.

headlines.title: 'THREE MEN AND A BABY' TOPS BOX OFFICE
headlines.summary: The Tom Selleck-Steve Guttenberg-Ted Danson comedy, released Thanksgiving week, is the season's runaway hit and is packing theaters into December.

headlines.title: US NAVAL ESCORTS CONTINUE IN PERSIAN GULF
headlines.summary: American warships continue shepherding reflagged Kuwaiti tankers through the Persian Gulf as the Iran-Iraq war's tanker war grinds on into its fourth year.

announcements: CURRENT EVENTS FORUM: INF Treaty signing discussion -- GO NEWS. Share your take on the Washington summit.
CB Simulator: Channel 8 is the summit channel this week. All handles welcome.
Scheduled maintenance: the service will be unavailable Sunday 2:00-6:00 AM Eastern for system upgrades.
cb_topics: Reagan just signed a treaty with Gorbachev. Never thought I would see the day.
'Trust, but verify.' Reagan's Russian is getting a workout.
Those Pershing IIs are finally coming out of West Germany.
The Dow has clawed back a lot since October. My retirement account thanks the summit.
Got OS/2 on the PS/2 at work. Multitasking! Sort of.
Three Men and a Baby this weekend -- the theater was packed.
market_notes: Stocks steady in light holiday trading after a seven-week climb back from Black Monday.
Defense shares mixed as the INF Treaty starts dismantling intermediate missile programs.

on_this_day.title: INF Treaty signed at the White House (December 8, 1987)
on_this_day.summary: Reagan and Gorbachev agree to eliminate an entire class of nuclear missiles, with on-site inspection.

on_this_day.title: John Lennon shot in New York (December 8, 1980)
on_this_day.summary: The former Beatle is killed outside the Dakota apartment building.

on_this_day.title: United States declares war on Japan (December 8, 1941)
on_this_day.summary: Congress answers the Pearl Harbor attack a day after Britain's declaration.

1989-10-17.label: Loma Prieta earthquake

headlines.title: 6.9 QUAKE ROCKS BAY AREA, INTERRUPTS WORLD SERIES
headlines.summary: A magnitude 6.9 earthquake struck the San Francisco Bay Area at 5:04 p.m. Pacific, moments before Game 3 of the World Series at Candlestick Park. The ABC broadcast went dark as the stadium shook; the game between the Athletics and the Giants was postponed.

headlines.title: CYPRESS FREEWAY COLLAPSE KILLS DOZENS
headlines.summary: A double-deck section of the Cypress Street Viaduct on Interstate 880 in Oakland pancaked onto the lower deck, crushing cars in the deadliest single collapse of the quake.

headlines.title: BAY BRIDGE SECTION FALLS; BRIDGE CLOSED
headlines.summary: A 50-foot section of the upper deck of the San Francisco-Oakland Bay Bridge collapsed, and the bridge -- the Bay Area's busiest commuter link -- is closed indefinitely.

headlines.title: FIRES BURN IN SAN FRANCISCO'S MARINA DISTRICT
headlines.summary: Broken gas mains ignited fires in the Marina District, where liquefied soil toppled homes off their foundations. Firefighters are drafting water from the bay as hydrants run dry.

headlines.title: WORLD SERIES POSTPONED AFTER QUAKE
headlines.summary: Commissioner Fay Vincent postponed the Series with Oakland leading San Francisco two games to none. Engineers are inspecting Candlestick Park, where concrete fell from the stadium's upper baffle, and no date has been set to resume play.

headlines.title: BUSH DECLARES MAJOR DISASTER IN CALIFORNIA
headlines.summary: President Bush declared a major disaster area, freeing federal aid for the Bay Area. The governor has activated the National Guard as search teams work through the night.

headlines.title: PHONE NETWORK JAMMED; HAM RADIO FILLS GAP
headlines.summary: Telephone circuits into the Bay Area are jammed with callers seeking news of relatives. Amateur radio emergency nets are passing health-and-welfare traffic for shelters and hospitals.

headlines.title: QUAKE DAMAGE ESTIMATES CLIMB INTO BILLIONS
headlines.summary: Early damage estimates are climbing into the billions of dollars as insurers and engineers survey collapsed freeways, burned blocks, and damaged downtown high-rises across the Bay Area.

headlines.title: 'LOOK WHO'S TALKING' TOPS BOX OFFICE
headlines.summary: The John Travolta-Kirstie Alley comedy, which opened Friday, is the weekend's number one film nationwide.

headlines.title: THRIFT CLEANUP GAINS STEAM
headlines.summary: Federal regulators are seizing failed savings and loans at a record pace under this summer's bailout law, with hundreds of insolvent thrifts headed for resolution.

announcements: NEWS FORUM: Bay Area earthquake coverage -- GO NEWS. Members in the Bay Area, please check in when you can.
CB Simulator: Channel 17 is the emergency-information channel today. Real traffic only, please.
Scheduled maintenance: the service will be unavailable Sunday 2:00-6:00 AM Eastern for system upgrades.
cb_topics: I was watching Game 3 when the screen went green. Al Michaels said it best.
The Cypress freeway pancaked. I drive that stretch every day.
Ham operators are passing health-and-welfare traffic. God bless the hams.
Bush declared a disaster area. FEMA is on the way.
My cousin in Santa Cruz says the house is fine but the chimney is in the yard.
They will play ball again in ten days. Right now, baseball does not matter.
market_notes: Insurance shares under pressure as Bay Area damage estimates climb into the billions.
Wall Street watches California; New York trading desks report no disruption to operations.

on_this_day.title: Loma Prieta earthquake strikes the Bay Area (October 17, 1989)
on_this_day.summary: The 6.9 quake kills 63, collapses the Cypress Viaduct and a Bay Bridge section, and interrupts the World Series.

on_this_day.title: Mother Teresa awarded the Nobel Peace Prize (October 17, 1979)
on_this_day.summary: The Missionaries of Charity founder is honored for her work with the poor.

on_this_day.title: Albert Einstein arrives in the United States (October 17, 1933)
on_this_day.summary: The physicist lands to take up a post at Princeton's new Institute for Advanced Study.

1990-04-24.label: Hubble launched

headlines.title: DISCOVERY LIFTS HUBBLE INTO ORBIT
headlines.summary: Space Shuttle Discovery lifted off from Launch Pad 39B at 8:33 a.m. Eastern this morning carrying the Hubble Space Telescope. Commander Loren Shriver and pilot Charles Bolden lead the five-person crew; mission specialists Steven Hawley, Bruce McCandless, and Kathryn Sullivan will deploy the telescope tomorrow with the shuttle's robot arm.

headlines.title: WINDOW ON THE EARLY UNIVERSE
headlines.summary: The 24,000-pound observatory's 2.4-meter mirror should see ten times sharper than any ground telescope, letting astronomers peer billions of years back toward the birth of the universe. First images are expected within weeks.

headlines.title: A JOINT US-EUROPEAN VENTURE
headlines.summary: Hubble is a joint NASA-European Space Agency project more than a decade in the making, delayed by years of budget battles and the post-Challenger shuttle grounding. Scientists from 15 nations have observing time booked.

headlines.title: SOVIET BLOCKADE SQUEEZES LITHUANIA
headlines.summary: Moscow has cut oil and gas to Lithuania, which declared independence from the Soviet Union last month. President Bush has urged Gorbachev to negotiate with the Baltic republic.

headlines.title: BUSH AND GORBACHEV SET JUNE SUMMIT
headlines.summary: The White House confirmed that President Bush and Mikhail Gorbachev will meet in Washington in late May for their first full summit, with arms control and Lithuania expected to dominate.

headlines.title: EXXON VALDEZ SPILL: ONE YEAR LATER
headlines.summary: A year after the Exxon Valdez ran aground in Prince William Sound, cleanup crews are returning to Alaska's beaches for a second summer. Exxon's spill costs have topped a billion dollars and the lawsuits are just beginning.

headlines.title: WINDOWS 3.0 DRAWS RAVE PREVIEWS
headlines.summary: Microsoft's Windows 3.0, due in stores next month, is winning glowing advance reviews from the computer press for its speed, icons, and Program Manager. Dealers expect it to finally make Windows a mainstream product.

headlines.title: 'PRETTY WOMAN' TOPS BOX OFFICE
headlines.summary: The Richard Gere-Julia Roberts fairy tale, in its fifth week, remains the nation's number one film.

headlines.title: NBA PLAYOFFS TIP OFF THURSDAY
headlines.summary: The NBA regular season wrapped up Sunday, and the playoffs open Thursday with the Lakers, Pistons, and Bulls among the favorites.

headlines.title: COBE DATA BACKS BIG BANG MODEL
headlines.summary: Scientists analyzing data from NASA's COBE satellite say the cosmic background radiation matches the Big Bang's predictions with stunning precision -- a landmark result announced earlier this year.

announcements: SPACE FORUM: Hubble deployment discussion -- GO SPACE. First light images are expected within weeks.
CB Simulator: Channel 24 is the astronomy channel tonight. Bring your star charts.
Scheduled maintenance: the service will be unavailable Sunday 2:00-6:00 AM Eastern for system upgrades.
cb_topics: Discovery carried a school-bus-sized telescope into orbit this morning. Let that sink in.
Ten times sharper than anything on the ground. Palomar is going to feel old.
Over a billion dollars for a mirror in space. Worth every penny, I say.
Kathryn Sullivan is on this crew -- she walked in space back in '84.
Windows 3.0 next month. Finally, a Windows worth installing.
Pretty Woman last weekend -- Julia Roberts is going to be huge.
market_notes: Wall Street mixed as the week opens; aerospace shares steady after the flawless launch.
Oil prices stable as Alaskan cleanup costs weigh on Exxon a year after the Valdez spill.

on_this_day.title: Hubble Space Telescope launched aboard Discovery (April 24, 1990)
on_this_day.summary: The 2.4-meter observatory is deployed the next day, beginning its mission above Earth's atmosphere.

on_this_day.title: Library of Congress founded (April 24, 1800)
on_this_day.summary: Congress approves $5,000 for books for the new Capitol library.

on_this_day.title: Cosmonaut Vladimir Komarov killed in Soyuz 1 (April 24, 1967)
on_this_day.summary: The first in-flight spaceflight fatality occurs when Soyuz 1's parachutes fail on re-entry.
